I used the following tutorial to install rApache on Ubuntu 11.04:

http://www.zh-cn.org/en/2011/05/19/english-setting-up-a-rapache-environment/

is that the configuration file in Step #4 assumes that the www folder
in my home directory has files such as processform.r, helloworld.r,
sendBin.r, and test.R.  In order to get the apache server to accept
this configuration, I had to comment out all portions that of this
file that referred to this www folder.  I have posted my commented out
configuration file at the end of this post.

I am wondering if the rApache installation puts those files elsewhere
and I need to move these files into a www folder that I create.  Or do
I need to download and/or create these files from somewhere else?

as code.  In that case, the r-snippets do work.  If I then add a .html
extension to the file, the html code will correctly render, but the r-
snippet throws an error.  Any ideas?

Thanks in advance for any help somebody could provide on this.
Cheers,
Markus

messages.body_plain:
Hi
I created a web based tool that uses RApache. My web tool is working
perfectly except that it is having some efficiency issues. I am trying
to explain what I need and whether it is possible or not.

Suppose I am doing following calculations in R
1. dataFile = read.csv("testFolder/dataFile.csv", header=TRUE);
2. doCalculations(dataFile);

Every time a user opens the page, both of the lines above will be
executed. Executing line 1 takes around 30 second that is too much
while calculation takes just 3 seconds in my case.

Loading the same file for each user is something which I want to avoid
and I guess there might be some way to skip this step.

Is it possible to write code and some how avoid loading the file? Can
"RSourceOnStartup" or "REvalOnStarup" help me somehow? And how to
receive "dataFile"?

Thanks a lot.
Fahim

messages.body_plain:
Well, you can save CSV file to R binary format (.RData, .rda), and load it via REvalOnStartup. If your data is generated dynamically (via some script or smth), you should convert it to binary format, hence load it. If you're emotionally attached to CSV format, you may want to provide colClasses argument in read.csv function. It will speed up whole process, since you will skip looping over each column to determine appropriate column class.

Also, take a look at this link: http://stackoverflow.com/q/4756989/457898

Thanks a lot for your reply.

My Csv files are generated  once every 3 months and I do not care whether it is in csv format or .Rdata format, I just want my work to be done. filenames = list.files(path = "/home/fahim/webRugit/mm9/outData", pattern = '.Rdata$', all.files = FALSE, full.names = TRUE, ignore.case = FALSE)

Thanks and regards
Fahim

Ad 1. - perhaps you meant brew is an alternative to Sweave. Well... brew is templating convention for R. It works on textual files, so it's more flexible than Sweave. Sweave, OTOH, has many advantages over brew - it can handle many things in the background (graphs, command input, etc.)

Ad 2. - let's assume that you've already prepared Sweave file, and you only want to grab stuff from your data and process Sweave file - piece of cake:

> Sweave("input_file.Rnw")
> tools::texi2dvi("input_file.tex", pdf = TRUE)

Voila!

Of course, you need to take care about background stuff... this is only a sweave webapp in a nutshell! =)

messages.body_plain:
You should upgrade your R installation in order to get up-to-date packages. Why would you choose RJSONIO over rjson - that one's easy: speed. RJSONIO is faster (at least they advertise so in official documentation). AFAIK RJSONIO was hosted on omegahat before it was uploaded on CRAN, so all you have to do is to grab gzipped tarball and install package from local hard drive.

Take a look at http://www.omegahat.org/RJSONIO/
Once you download the package archive, run:
install.packages("<pkg name>", type = "source", repos = NULL)

but you should really update your R installation, since RJSONIO is now on CRAN. Basic functionallity is pretty similar: toJSON() and fromJSON() methods exist in both packages.

About data structure: keep in mind that RApache provides POST superglobal, much like PHP. It is a list. All you have to do is to tweak the list, or (even better) tweak the data on the client side. You may want to use some JS library. My choice is jQuery. Take a look at jQuery form plugin: http://jquery.malsup.com/form/ - this should be helpful

Or you can use vanilla jQuery. In a nutshell, you should pass POST parameters as JSON string - i.e. you should encode them before you submit the form, then decode/deparse the JSON string on the server side.

So there... That's pretty much it.

Good luck! =)
